clue.text: I must get into dynamic core and abs exercise

indicators.note: something that must get into another has to be placed inside it
dynamic means full of energy and movement, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, the rest of the anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gym instructor insists you need a lively session working your core and stomach muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like it joins two parts of the body, but both words are fodder and only the last word, 'exercise', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobics is a form of rhythmic physical workout, often done in classes, so it is a type of exercise.

clue.text: Principal setter's record collection

parts.note: arch- as in archenemy means chief or principal
the setter refers to themselves as I, and 'setter's' here is 'setter has', giving I'VE

explanation.surface: The chief puzzle compiler shows off a cherished stack of vinyl albums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record collection' suggests vinyl, but here it means a store of documents. The 's is read as 'has', so the setter's becomes I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a gathered store of historical documents and files, literally a collection of records.

clue.text: Small jumper belonging to me is generously proportioned

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, and the short form of the word makes it small
the possessive for something that belongs to me

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their little sweater is actually rather large.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper in British English is a sweater, which the surface leans on; the wordplay wants a creature that jumps, the kangaroo, shortened to ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roomy has plenty of space inside, so it is spacious, ample and generously proportioned.

clue.text: County forbids introduction of deer here, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of deer
taken as written, part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A local council bans bringing deer into the area, which seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is FORBIDS plus D plus HERE, twelve letters in all; 'here' reads as part of the scene but is used letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire is a county in the east of England, north of London, whose county town is Bedford.

clue.text: King Charles is beginning to prepare snack using potato

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of prepare

explanation.surface: The monarch is starting to make himself a potato-based nibble.
explanation.walkthrough: CR is the royal cipher of a King Charles, from the Latin Carolus Rex. A crisp is the British word for what North Americans call a potato chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp is a thin fried slice of potato sold in bags, a classic British savoury snack.

clue.text: Recognise geek from the back

indicators.note: reading from the back means starting at the end, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a wonk is a studious or nerdy person, a geek

explanation.surface: You can spot a nerd even when you only see them from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: WONK, a policy nerd or swot, is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To know someone or something can mean to identify it on sight, the same sense as recognise.

clue.text: Falls over in North America?

parts.note: surface reading: someone tumbles to the ground while visiting the continent
setter's reading: the famous waterfalls on the border between Canada and the United States

explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb with 'over' attached, but it is the noun, as in a waterfall, and 'over' places them on top of the continent's map.
explanation.definitionFit: The great cataracts on the river between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario are the best-known waterfalls on the continent.

clue.text: Large animal's audible sound of distress

indicators.note: audible means able to be heard, so what matters is what the ear catches, not the spelling

parts.note: a wail is a long cry of grief or pain

explanation.surface: A big creature lets out a cry of pain that everyone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay: a wail and a whale are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The whale is a huge marine mammal, the blue whale being the biggest creature that has ever lived.

clue.text: Notice vice-president gathering troops for initial mission

parts.note: an ad is a notice, as in a small advertisement
JD Vance became US vice-president in 2025
a party is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A deputy leader is seen mustering soldiers to start an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering troops' reads as one action by the vice-president, but 'gathering' gives PARTY and 'troops' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance party is a small group sent ahead of the main force to scout or prepare the ground.

clue.text: Obscure album plugged by singer Reed

indicators.note: a hole plugged by something has that thing stuffed inside it

parts.note: an album released on compact disc
Lou Reed was the singer of the Velvet Underground

explanation.surface: A little-known record gets promoted by the rock musician Lou Reed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective describing the album, but it is a verb meaning to hide or blur.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud an issue is to make it murky or harder to see clearly, which is to obscure it.

clue.text: State where Prince Harry spent nine months?

parts.note: the place Harry spent those months was inside someone
nine months is a pregnancy, and Harry's mother was Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A question about which American state the prince lived in for most of a year.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine months are a pregnancy, so Harry was IN DIANA, his mother Princess Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the US, in the Midwest, with Indianapolis as its capital.

clue.text: Unfriendly, expensive public relations leaves

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: pricey is an informal word for costly
PR is the usual abbreviation for public relations

explanation.surface: A cold, overpriced publicity firm is quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a noun, as in foliage, but it is the verb: PR departs from PRICEY.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy manner is cold and hostile, so an icy person is distinctly unwelcoming.

clue.text: Gold leaf coats Chinese children's home

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: a coat goes all around what it covers, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
the Han are the majority ethnic group of China

explanation.surface: Gold leaf is applied over a Chinese family's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold leaf' reads as one gilding material, but it splits into two pieces, and 'coats' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is an institution that houses and cares for children without parents.

clue.text: Make concrete dome by using mixer?

indicators.note: a mixer churns its contents together, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Building a concrete dome with the help of a cement mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' sits naturally beside the cement mixer, but in the definition it means tangible; 'by' looks like a link word and is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody an idea is to give it a tangible, visible form, which is making an abstract thing concrete.

clue.text: Relatively tasteless, second-rate slice of bacon?

parts.note: a B grade is second-rate, below A
a rasher is a thin slice of bacon

explanation.surface: A complaint that a cheap piece of bacon has hardly any flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteless' suggests food without flavour, but it means vulgar, and 'relatively' asks for a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means showy and lacking in refinement, so brasher is comparatively vulgar or showing worse taste.

clue.text: Dash off to swim after end of Friends

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the sitcom title
the crawl is a swimming stroke, and to crawl is to swim it

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off for a swim as soon as the TV sitcom Friends finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash off' reads as hurrying away, but it means writing something hastily; the swim comes after the S in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash off a note is to write it quickly and carelessly, and to scrawl is to write in a hurried, messy hand.

clue.text: Gastronomic delicacy served up in Margaret's bolognese

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
the answer is found in the next words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the apostrophe and the word break

explanation.surface: A luxury seafood is dished up in Margaret's pasta sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' fits the restaurant scene, but in a down clue it means the letters are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobster is an expensive shellfish prized in fine dining, a classic luxury food.

clue.text: Stupidly short the adapter? That could kill you

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the last letter is dropped
doing something stupidly means getting it all wrong, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: the word without its final letter
taken as written, part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A warning about carelessly causing a short circuit in an electrical adapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like the electrical sense, short-circuit, but it clips the last letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is a dangerous place, vehicle or device likely to cause fatal accidents.

clue.text: Plan recruitment of American soldiers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a preliminary version or outline
second meaning: compulsory US military conscription

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single plan to enlist troops, but it holds two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a rough first version or plan, and in the US the draft is conscription into the armed forces.

clue.text: Leads in remake of Yojimbo are looking magnificent

indicators.note: leads are those at the front, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: The stars of a new version of Kurosawa's samurai film Yojimbo look splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' suggests the film's lead actors, but it means the leading letters of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal can mean splendid or fit for a king, as in a royal welcome, matching magnificent.

clue.text: Gossip initially about living in Great Britain

indicators.note: to live in a place is to be inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: GB is the standard abbreviation for Great Britain

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of about

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle, at first, concerns life in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', but it is the source of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To gab is to chatter idly, and gab is informal for talk or gossip.

clue.text: Soup's adhesive with unpleasant smell

parts.note: gum is a glue
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A bowl of soup is gluey and stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumbo is a thick stew-like soup from Louisiana, made with okra or file and seafood or meat.

clue.text: On the wrong path going around hot waste receptacle

indicators.note: going around something means encircling it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to go astray is to wander off the right route
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A lost traveller wanders round a smouldering rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' sits nicely beside a smoker's receptacle, but it is only the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is a small dish that collects cigarette ash and butts, a holder for smoking refuse.

clue.text: Right issue and terms of reference

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
to emit is to send out or issue

explanation.surface: A financial or legal phrase: a rights issue together with its defined terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right issue' echoes a 'rights issue' of shares, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the area of responsibility officially assigned to a person or committee, its scope of authority.

clue.text: Phrase checked by interpreter maybe

indicators.note: something checked is held back or contained, so it sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A translator might verify a particular expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked' reads as verified, but here it means held in, as in held in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a word or expression used for a particular thing, so it can stand for a phrase.

clue.text: Try interrupting sportsperson who's focused on the drama?

definitions.note: a relative clause describing a person, standing for the noun

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a player takes part in a sport
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: An attempt to distract an athlete who is caught up in a theatrical scene, perhaps a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama' suggests on-field histrionics, but it means the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgoer is someone who regularly attends theatre performances, an audience member watching plays.
